alerts.title: Rising creatinine and declining eGFR on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines state that in patients on TDF, it is important to check creatinine (eGFR), as intercurrent illnesses with dehydration or sepsis may cause renal deterioration. Patient's creatinine has progressively risen from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m². TDF is a known cause of proximal tubular toxicity and declining eGFR. Urinalysis showing protein 1+ supports possible TDF nephrotoxicity. Against drug attribution: no oedema, stable weight, and no acute intercurrent illness today. However, the steady 6-year upward trend is concerning even without an acute trigger. Ibuprofen use 2–3 times weekly may compound renal risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate for TDF nephrotoxicity; consider renal-protective alternatives or dose adjustment. Assess ibuprofen contribution and advise limiting NSAID use. Repeat creatinine and urinalysis promptly.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for today's visit despite abnormal renal markers (creatinine 1.4, eGFR 52, proteinuria) and a 6-year creatinine trend warranting clinical action. Guidelines indicate TDF patients require renal monitoring and that intercurrent illness can worsen renal function. The absence of any plan represents a guideline deviation and monitoring gap. Additionally, VL monitoring at 6-monthly intervals is appropriate per guidelines for patients on DTG-based ART, and the latest VL is suppressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment addressing renal function decline and proteinuria. Formulate plan for renal monitoring, NSAID reduction, and possible TDF review. Confirm VL monitoring schedule.

alerts.title: Frequent ibuprofen use compounding renal risk
alerts.message: Patient takes ibuprofen 400 mg 2–3 times weekly for headaches over the past 6 months. NSAIDs can reduce renal perfusion via prostaglandin inhibition, worsening renal function. Combined with TDF nephrotoxicity risk and already declining eGFR (52 mL/min/1.73m²), concurrent NSAID use compounds kidney injury risk. No guideline excerpt directly addresses NSAID-TDF interaction, but the renal monitoring guidance for TDF patients supports evaluating all contributors to renal decline. Alternative analgesia such as paracetamol should be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to reduce or discontinue ibuprofen; recommend paracetamol for headache relief. Investigate headache cause. Monitor renal function if NSAID use continues.
